lore: Pons Index is a moving basket of the ten largest eligible tokens launched through the Pons ecosystem. Part of its creator rewards is recycled through that basket and distributed in recurring epochs, so the index changes as the ecosystem's leaders change.

Russell is Brian Armstrong's Akita Inu, best known for walking down the aisle at the Coinbase co-founder's wedding. The community adopted him as an unofficial Base mascot and kept the token alive through a community takeover after its original developer left.
Prologue is Fables' dynamic-fee ve(3,3) exchange on Robinhood Chain, built with Uniswap v4; its launch token is intended to redeem for the governance token at TGE.
Lil Uni uses the unicorn hidden in Uniswap's 404 page as its mascot and presents itself as an unaffiliated Robinhood Chain community takeover.
The Council is based on a fictional online cult that spread through viral YouTube Shorts and became a recurring internet character universe.

Pistacio began as a new street-nicknamed character drawn by meme artist Marcello. The community tokenized the drawing and routed creator fees back to him; Marcello acknowledged the coin and followed it with more Pistacio artwork, turning a one-off sketch into a developing character.
BATON is a community derivative of Baton Corporation, Pump.fun's former legal identity; the later token is unaffiliated and has documented coordination concerns.
Anton Palkin's six-agent Grok desk splits filings, earnings, sectors, insider trades and social chatter into one nightly market brief.
GEORGE trades under the name Real Kid, though its character origin and any outside catalyst remain unverified.

FIH is a community-made meme based on one of artist Marcell's drawings. Marcell disclosed that someone made the coin, shared creator fees with him, and that he would draw memes for the community if it survived; he explicitly warned buyers to invest at their own risk.
PONS is the reference token for Pons, a launch-and-trade protocol on Robinhood Chain; its documentation says launcher liquidity graduates into the same pool with LP locked automatically.

INDEX turns a meme token into an automated stock-reward system on Robinhood Chain. A trading fee buys tokenized shares such as major tech stocks and distributes them proportionally to eligible holders, giving the meme a live basket-of-stocks mechanic.
Jimothy is a real short-spined Seattle raccoon who became a neighborhood and online community mascot; the official site publishes this exact contract.

CyberLeek grew out of the anonymous GTA 6 leak campaign that watermarked unreleased footage with the character and this exact Solana mint. The group framed the stunt as a protest against digital preorders, paid content and games disappearing when servers shut down.
GrokBot uses an AI-bot identity, but no working product, established origin or outside catalyst could be verified.

Down to Finance turns a basket of assets or an active strategy into one on-chain token. Its decentralized ETF system lets anyone create a basket, while DTF holders can stake for protocol fees; the builder says the design revisits Olympus-style mechanics without claiming an official Olympus affiliation.

MARTIANS grew from Robinhood co-founder Vlad Tenev replying to Elon Musk about Mars colonization. The community cast the pair as 'the first Martians,' then extended the joke through Vlad's own reference to a Mars Trilogy colonist who shares his name.
MEMESTOCK styles itself as a fixed-supply 'memetic common stock' quoted in GMEB; its fee mechanism distributes GMEB to eligible holders, and it explicitly says it is unaffiliated with GameStop.
Exact-contract research identifies BRODIE as Robinhood Dog, but found no reliable character origin or independent catalyst.
TOKABU is the long-running 'Spirit of Gambling' mascot for casino-style crypto speculation; exact-contract exchange announcements corroborate the identity.

MARTIANS turns Elon Musk's recurring jokes about being a Martian into a community identity for future Mars settlers. Its exact-contract site presents the coin as an independent Solana meme movement built around Mars, technology and interplanetary culture, with no official connection to Musk or his companies.

Sue is the kitten construction workers rescued from beneath a Komatsu excavator at an Ohio job site. The crew kept her and named her Komatsu, usually shortened to Sue; Komatsu later sent the tiny hard hat and safety vest that turned her into the internet's construction cat.

PACK is the two-wolves idea turned into a token: six permanently locked pools pair it with tokenized stocks, while four pair it with Robinhood-chain memes. Buys feed market buybacks and deeper liquidity; sells burn PACK, so trading continually strengthens or reduces the supply.

HOOD10 is an experimental index token for Robinhood Chain. Each trade pays a 5% tax; its documentation says 4% is used to buy the ten largest eligible tokens by pool liquidity, then distribute those assets to holders at the end of each epoch.
LOOM has an active market and community footprint, but its original project story and current catalyst remain unverified.

18bro is the black cat that stole a bag of chips from a Hong Kong 7-Eleven and triggered a citywide online hunt. After the cat was found, the store adopted it and named it Eighteen Bro after the markings on its head, then began treating the former snack thief as an official mascot.

Zoe came from a character post shared inside an anti-AI-art community, with the coin appearing only seconds after the original material. The unusual part of the story is that the token and its fandom began forming almost simultaneously, before the community had settled on a wider backstory for Zoe.
Exact-contract research found no reliable origin story or independent catalyst for this BSC token.

SEYONGPARK is a playful tribute to Se Yong Park, co-founder of the Fomo trading app. Its exact-contract site turns him into an entire surreal amusement park, filling the grounds with duck rides, slides, fountains and playground equipment shaped in his likeness.

POLYCAT is the low-poly cat eating ice cream that went viral through short-form edits. Its deliberately rough early-3D look carries the joke, mixing game-era nostalgia with a sad little cat that can be understood without any caption.

LAPEACE comes from Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed's Minecraft Hardcore stream. Speed thought they had found diamonds, but Kai softly corrected him with 'that's lapis'; his pronunciation sounded like 'la peace,' and editors recast him as a calm old philosopher until the clip became a viral TikTok and Reels format.

PONSBOT is the token attached to an independent Robinhood Chain wallet and launch tool built around X posts. The bot lets users claim a wallet, trade, send tokens and create new launches through short commands without leaving the social feed.
Exact-contract research identifies WINFREY as Winfrey The Orca, but found no independently verifiable animal or character origin.

Dundun was a viral Douyin cat whose owner says it died after a routine neutering was mishandled by a pet hospital. The clinic allegedly could not provide basic veterinary credentials and offered another cat as compensation, turning the token into a community campaign demanding accountability for Dundun.

ENCORE formed around Evelyn Chen, an 18-year-old builder documenting her interest in blockchain. She publicly acknowledged receiving the token's creator fees, which turned the coin into a community-backed bet on a young developer rather than a formal Encore Labs launch.
SpaceX Opossum is a community space-meme runner; the exact contract is indexed publicly, but no official SpaceX connection or original character source could be verified.
BADGERS riffs on Mr Weebl's endlessly looping 2003 'Badger Badger Badger' animation, one of the early web's most recognizable viral memes; this token is a community derivative.
TITAN presents itself as part of the Titan.fun fair-launch scene on Robinhood Chain, though the public site does not clearly certify this exact token as an official platform asset.
HOOKR is the token behind a no-code Uniswap v4 hook launchpad, letting creators add anti-snipe fees, burns, LP rewards and other programmable mechanics without writing Solidity.

CP turns 'Crypto President' into a two-person BNB meme. The community pairs Changpeng Zhao's old 'Crypto President!' line with Trump, casting the two figures as crypto power and political power sharing the same initials.
BAOBAO traded like a fresh BNB meme, but no reliable source tied this exact contract to an established character or project story.

MEAT riffs on the new tech insult 'meat proxy': a person who blindly forwards AI-generated work without reading or understanding it. The phrase escaped developer circles in August and became a wider joke about humans acting as little more than relays for chatbots.
NITTER borrows the name of the privacy-friendly alternative X/Twitter front end. The meme connection is clear, but no official link to the open-source Nitter project was found.
This BNB runner uses the Chinese rendering of Trump, but no verified campaign, creator, or specific news trigger could be tied to the contract.
IF became a community takeover after the original developer disappeared, turning the simple 'what if?' hook into a holder-run Robinhood Chain meme.
BASENOUN is a self-aware Base-chain noun meme whose own listing calls it a high-effort coin and explicitly says it was not launched by the Base team.

WEBSITE treats web-page space as tradeable digital real estate. People can buy headline, button and ad slots on the live page, while the project records sales and routes part of that activity back to token holders.
This Chinese-named BNB runner passed on market action, but searches did not uncover a trustworthy origin story or creator trail for the exact contract.
WIRE is a Twitter-native trading bot on Robinhood Chain: users tweet natural-language commands to trade tokenized stocks such as NVDA, TSLA and AAPL through a self-custodial wallet flow.
Lao Wu comes from a viral Douyin cat clip where the meow sounds like the Chinese name 'Lao Wu'; the community joke says one cat meows, but a whole group chants Lao Wu.
LINK is an unofficial Zelda parody imagining the hero leaving Hyrule, putting down the shield and taking the long road home; its site clearly disclaims any Nintendo affiliation.

Veggie Traders imagines 4,444 fruit-and-vegetable characters as tiny autonomous stock pickers. Owners activate an NFT by burning VEGGIES, after which its built-in strategy chooses from tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain and any funded harvest follows the NFT.

GMEOW turns the cat-style greeting repeatedly used across crypto X into a BNB meme, with the community pointing to past uses by Binance and other cat-loving accounts rather than claiming an official affiliation.

PNUTS traded as a cult-style Solana community play after Siris publicly joined the group. That confirms visible trader attention around the contract, although it is not a separate product or news catalyst.

SABL is Sable Network's community token, launched after the compute project reversed its earlier no-token position. The team is unusually explicit that it is a high-risk meme asset: it does not pay for compute, gate the platform, provide governance or share revenue.

AURA turns the internet's 'aura points' joke into a Solana mascot coin. The meme treats every impressive or embarrassing moment like a game score, with people gaining or losing imaginary social-cool points in real time.
PONGO became an early mascot inside the Pons ecosystem, where the community presents it as the first original meme to complete the platform's bonding process.

SPARKY cleared the trading filters, but its attached evidence resolved to a generic block-explorer page—and even referenced a different mint. There is not enough trustworthy context to assign this contract a story yet.
DICKCOIN is a deliberately crude ticker meme on Solana. The linked pages establish the market, but they do not reveal an original creator, character, or event behind it.

PANTS brings back a dog character whose whole joke is that it started wearing pants in 2016 and never stopped. The project turned that old visual gag into a Solana community coin launched through Ansem's launchpad.

TOADS is built around Poet Toads, a collection from the long-running Solana typewriter artist known as degen poet. The character sits inside the artist's broader handmade, literary NFT world rather than being a random frog ticker invented for the day's move.
DOGGYSTYLE formed around a dog character named Frankie, with the community turning the simple name reveal into the mascot behind the coin.

BUTTHOLE takes one deliberately stupid joke—there is no fart without a butthole—and treats it like a full Solana brand. The absurdly literal pitch is the product here, and the official site leans into it without pretending there is deeper utility.

Sparky is the dog character used as the default model in Tesla's AI companion material. The meme grew from people spotting the name and matching it to Tesla's dog-mode toys and pet imagery; the token is a community adaptation of that character, not a Tesla-issued asset.

9gnosis is an AI experiment built as a shared computer inhabited by autonomous agents. Each agent lives behind a file that people can query, turning the machine into a small persistent digital society rather than a conventional chatbot app.
FRUG is a hand-drawn frog by Big Frugowski made for traders who have survived rugs. The character turns that shared pain into the joke: rugs hurt, but the people who stayed remember the culture.

APP came from Pump.fun co-founder Alon repeatedly ending posts with 'Sent from my Pumpfun App.' The signature spread as a platform-native joke, and this coin turned that suddenly recognizable footer into the meme.

DOOM combines the game's 30-year nostalgia with direct support from original Doom and Doom II level designer Sandy Petersen. He publicly joined the community, shared the contract and promoted its browser-based play-to-earn version of the game.

CyberLeek started as a neon cyberpunk leek character whose TikTok account was accused of being fake. The backlash became the joke: supporters launched Justice for CyberLeek and used the character's own site to rally the community around the mascot.

Gucci Morty began as an edit of Morty Smith wearing a Gucci shirt, skinny jeans and a fresh haircut. The joke recast the usually nervous character as impossibly cool and full of aura, then spread through TikTok, Instagram and X edits before this Solana community turned the trend into a coin.

HUH comes from the reaction meme of Ben, the wide-eyed cat whose confused face is paired with a perfectly timed 'huh?' sound. The clip became a universal reply to baffling posts across TikTok and X, and this BNB coin is the community's version of that recognizable cat.

LSP is tied to Lesbian Space Princess, the Australian animated sci-fi comedy that unexpectedly became a TikTok and X battleground in August 2026. Arguments over the film, parody edits and the 'Just This Once' fandom truce pushed it into meme culture, and this Solana coin was launched around that viral wave.

STONK is the fee token behind StonkFun, a launchpad where new coins can trade against tokenized stocks and other assets instead of only SOL. Platform revenue is used for market buybacks and burns, while an optional reward mode routes a transfer tax back to holders.

ROBINVAULT began as the first token deployed through Emblem Vault's Robinhood Chain launchpad. Creator Jake Gallen treated it as a live social experiment for new Emblem Terminal features, then burned nearly half the supply to make the token deflationary.

JUGGERNAUT grew out of a meme Robinhood co-founder Vlad Tenev shared before Robinhood Chain launched: the comic-book character hugging him on Wall Street beneath a Robinhood sign. The community later put that image onchain as an unofficial tribute.

OBS is the token behind Obscura, a self-custodial execution layer built to route crypto and tokenized-stock trades across centralized and decentralized venues. Its pitch is private best-price execution, with part of the trading economics returned through its swap-to-earn model.
